note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of known low-grade prostate cancer with rising PSA and high-risk MRI findings to determine optimal management strategy.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. The patient is a 55-year-old office administrator who lives with his partner. He has a history of hypertension managed with amlodipine, lisinopril, and metoprolol. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 10. He is a non-smoker, consumes 25 units of alcohol weekly, and enjoys hiking on weekends. He recently attended an audiology appointment for a hearing test. He expresses anxiety about medical procedures, which has been noted in prior visits. His PSA has risen steadily from 1.6 ng/mL in June 2023 to 4.2 ng/mL in February 2025.

On DRE, the prostate is symmetrically enlarged without palpable nodules or asymmetry, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with a BMI of 26.3. Blood pressure is 145/77 mmHg and heart rate is 76 bpm. No peripheral edema or lymphadenopathy is noted.

admin: Patient anxious about procedures — allocate extra consult time.
